title: Flat finitely presented algebras are pseudo-coherent over every polynomial presentation
statement: Let $R\to C$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $n\geq0$ and let $\pi:P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow C$ be any surjective $R$-algebra homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then $C[0]$, regarded as a complex of $P$-modules via $\pi$, is pseudo-coherent in $D(P)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Equivalently it is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $P$-modules. Neither $R$ nor $C$ is assumed Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 067J, lemma-flat-finite-presentation-perfect, pseudo-coherence consequence; Tag 065H, lemma-relatively-pseudo-coherent, independence of the polynomial presentation. The meaning of pseudo-coherent ring map is definition-pseudo-coherent-perfect and definition-relatively-pseudo-coherent in the same file.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-finite-presentation-model] to $R\to C$. Rename its model rings $R_0,C_0$; it gives $R_0$ finitely presented over $\mathbf Z$, $C_0$ finitely presented and flat over $R_0$, and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $e:R\otimes_{R_0}C_0\cong C$. Its compatibility with the original map is essential. Every ideal of $\mathbf Z$ is generated by its least positive element, if it has one (division with remainder), and otherwise is zero. Hence $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian. Dropping the finite list of relations in a finite presentation shows finite type. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], first $R_0$ and then every finite polynomial algebra over $R_0$ are Noetherian. No Noetherian property of $R$ or $C$ is inferred.

source.place: Tag 067J, lemma-flat-finite-presentation-perfect, approximation and Noetherian-model paragraphs; algebra.tex, Tag 02JO (1) and Tag 00FN.

proof.text: Choose a finite presentation $\pi_0:P_0=R_0[z_1,\ldots,z_t]\twoheadrightarrow C_0$ using [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. The $P_0$-module $C_0$ is generated by $1$: for $c\in C_0$ lift $c$ to $p\in P_0$, so $c=p\cdot1$. Step 1 makes $P_0$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-resolution-noetherian] with ring $P_0$ and module $C_0$ to obtain an augmented exact complex $\cdots\to F_2\to F_1\to F_0\xrightarrow{\epsilon}C_0\to0$, where $F_i=P_0^{a_i}$ and $a_i$ is finite for every $i\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 00LP (2), lemma-resolution-by-finite-free; implements the finite-model pseudo-coherence in more-algebra.tex, Tag 067J.

proof.text: Regard this augmented complex as one of $R_0$-modules. Each $F_i$ is $R_0$-flat: its basis consists of a monomial of $P_0$ and one of the $a_i$ standard basis vectors; tensoring an injection with this direct sum gives the direct sum of that injection, which is injective coefficient by coefficient [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Set $K_{-1}=C_0$, $p_0=\epsilon$, and recursively $K_i=\ker p_i$; exactness factors the differential as a surjection $p_{i+1}:F_{i+1}\twoheadrightarrow K_i$ followed by $K_i\hookrightarrow F_i$. Thus $0\to K_i\to F_i\xrightarrow{p_i}K_{i-1}\to0$ is short exact for every $i\geq0$. Starting with the $R_0$-flat $K_{-1}=C_0$, induction using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ses-kernel-flat] makes every $K_i$ flat over $R_0$.

source.place: Tag 00HM, lemma-flat-ses, second assertion; explicit flat-syzygy realization of Tor independence used in more-algebra.tex, Tag 067J.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] to each short exact sequence of Step 3, with tensor factor the $R_0$-module $R$. Its quotient $K_{i-1}$ is flat, so $0	o R\otimes_{R_0}K_i	o R\otimes_{R_0}F_i	o R\otimes_{R_0}K_{i-1}	o0$ is exact. The tensored differential factors through the last surjection followed by the next injection, so its kernel is the image of $R\otimes K_i$, which is also the image of the preceding differential. The tensored augmentation is surjective. Put $P_1=R[z_1,\ldots,z_t]$. The monomial formula $r\otimes\sum_

The resulting exact finite-free $P_1$-resolution resolves $C$ via the presentation $\pi_1:P_1	woheadrightarrow C$ induced by $\pi_0$ and $e$. Surjectivity follows by writing each tensor as a sum of pure tensors and lifting its $C_0$ entries through $\pi_0$.

source.place: Tag 067J via Tag 067A, lemma-base-change-relative-pseudo-coherent; the tensor-exactness input is algebra.tex, Tag 00HL, lemma-flat-tor-zero.

proof.text: Place the finite-free terms of Step 4 in cochain degrees $-i$ and put zero in positive degrees. The augmentation to $C[0]$ induces an isomorphism on degree-zero cohomology because it is surjective with kernel the preceding image, and all other cohomology groups vanish by exactness. Hence [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] makes $C[0]$ pseudo-coherent for $\pi_1$. Apply [lem-sfb-polynomial-presentation-pseudocoherence-invariance] to the two surjective $R$-algebra maps $\pi_1:P_1\twoheadrightarrow C$ and the specified $\pi:P\twoheadrightarrow C$, with $K=C[0]$. This gives the required pseudo-coherence for $\pi$, and its finite-free formulation is precisely the cited definition. The construction allows $t=0$, $n=0$, zero rings, zero ranks and an unbounded negative tail.
